scrambled-egg-tomato-toast.text: About this meal: The extra egg whites give this breakfast a useful protein lift without adding another yolk. The tomato brings a fresh contrast to the buttery toast; it's a nice example of keeping a familiar breakfast while being thoughtful about the balance of protein and phosphorus.

apple-honey-porridge.text: About this meal: Warm apple and a little honey make these oats comforting without needing a large sweet topping. Milk and oats both contribute to the potassium and phosphorus figures, so this is a breakfast worth checking against your own advice if you monitor either nutrient. The oats also bring welcome fibre.

egg-tomato-onion-toast.text: About this meal: There's plenty of flavour in the softened tomato and onion, so this scramble doesn't need a salty sauce. Mixing extra whites with the whole egg adds protein without adding more yolks, which can be useful when you're paying attention to phosphorus as well as protein.

egg-white-chive-toast.text: About this meal: Egg whites and chives make a light, savoury filling with some protein and relatively little phosphorus from the eggs. Don't overlook the bread when checking salt: different loaves can vary quite a bit. A little chive goes a long way for flavour.

egg-pepper-onion-toast.text: About this meal: Sweet pepper and onion give the eggs plenty of character without bacon or a bottled sauce. The extra whites help make this a more substantial protein breakfast while keeping the number of yolks down. It's simple food, but there's a thoughtful balance behind it.

cinnamon-french-toast-with-jam.text: About this meal: The cinnamon and jam make this feel like a treat, while the egg-and-milk coating provides some protein. If you count carbohydrates, include the bread and jam together; the sweet topping isn't separate from the meal's total.

egg-tomato-onion-buttered-toast.text: About this meal: Gently cooked tomato and onion bring natural sweetness to the eggs and toast. You can get plenty of flavour here without adding ketchup or a salty seasoning. If potassium is something you monitor, the measured tomato portion is already included in the figures.

jam-butter-breakfast-toast.text: About this meal: Sometimes toast and marmalade is exactly what you fancy. It's mainly a carbohydrate-and-energy breakfast rather than a protein-rich one, so bear that in mind if your treatment plan calls for more protein earlier in the day. There's no need to make every breakfast do every job.

savoury-oats-egg-tomato-pepper.text: About this meal: Savoury porridge might sound unusual, but the egg, tomato and pepper make it more like a comforting breakfast bowl. The oats bring fibre and the added whites help with protein; the milk-free mixture also keeps the ingredients straightforward. Check the potassium and phosphorus totals if those are personal priorities.

apple-honey-french-toast.text: About this meal: Warm apple is a lovely topping for French toast, adding sweetness alongside the measured honey. The bread supplies most of the carbohydrate, while the egg-and-milk coating contributes protein. It's a useful reminder that a sweet-tasting breakfast can still have a varied nutritional profile.

blueberry-apple-toast.text: About this meal: Blueberries and apple do most of the work on flavour here, while cream cheese gives a smooth finish. Cream cheese is more about richness than protein, so don't count on a thicker spread to turn this into a high-protein breakfast. The fruit portions are included in the recorded potassium.

cinnamon-apple-toast.text: About this meal: Soft apple and cinnamon give ordinary toast a warm, pudding-like feel without needing much honey. This is a modest-protein breakfast, which may suit some eating plans better than others. If you've been asked to increase protein, it's worth planning for that elsewhere rather than just adding more spread.

strawberry-cream-cheese-toast.text: About this meal: Fresh strawberries give this toast its colour and a little sharpness against the cream cheese. The spread adds richness but not a great deal of protein. If you're comparing brands, it's worth looking at their salt content rather than assuming all cream cheeses are alike.

egg-pepper-breakfast-wrap.text: About this meal: Pepper and onion make the egg filling lively, while the extra egg whites give it more protein without another yolk. The tortilla and cream cheese can contribute salt, so the brands you choose matter as much as whether you add seasoning to the eggs.

apple-cinnamon-pancakes.text: About this meal: Apple and cinnamon give these pancakes a lot of flavour before the syrup goes on. The extra egg whites make them more substantial in protein than pancakes made from flour and milk alone. Enjoy the topping, but remember that the syrup is part of the carbohydrate total if you're counting it.

blueberry-yoghurt-toast.text: About this meal: The yoghurt adds creaminess and some protein, with blueberries bringing freshness and colour. Yoghurt also contributes potassium and phosphorus, so it's worth using the type and amount in the recipe when comparing the numbers with your own targets. Different dairy-free alternatives aren't nutritionally interchangeable.

egg-chive-muffin.text: About this meal: An egg-and-chive muffin makes a satisfying savoury start. Extra egg whites increase the protein without another yolk, while cream cheese gives the filling a softer texture. Muffin and spread brands can differ in salt, so check the label if that's something you're managing.

strawberry-maple-pancakes.text: About this meal: Strawberries lift these pancakes with freshness, so the maple syrup can stay a topping rather than doing all the flavouring. The batter includes extra whites for protein. If you count carbohydrates, the flour, fruit and syrup all contribute to the amount shown.

apple-cream-cheese-bagel.text: About this meal: A bagel is a substantial bread portion even when the topping looks light. Apple adds crunch and sweetness alongside the cream cheese, but the filling isn't particularly protein-rich. It's a handy breakfast to recognise as carbohydrate-led rather than assume the cheese makes it a protein meal.

egg-apple-breakfast-wrap.text: About this meal: Apple and cinnamon give this warm wrap a gentle sweetness, while egg and extra whites make it more filling than a fruit wrap alone. The tortilla supplies much of the carbohydrate. If phosphorus matters for you, the single yolk and cream cheese are worth considering alongside the total shown.

scrambled-egg-mushroom-toast.text: About this meal: Mushrooms give scrambled eggs a rich, savoury flavour, so there's little need for a salty sauce. The added egg whites provide extra protein without another yolk. Mushrooms also contribute potassium; the amount in this recipe has already been counted, so you can judge the whole serving rather than avoiding them automatically.

cornflakes-toast-jam.text: About this meal: This is a classic quick breakfast, but don't miss that it includes both cornflakes and toast. Together with the jam, they account for a sizeable carbohydrate portion. The milk adds protein and some potassium and phosphorus; it also matters if you're keeping a fluid record.

egg-onion-pepper-wrap.text: About this meal: Softened pepper and onion make a straightforward egg wrap taste like a cooked breakfast rather than a compromise. The tortilla is the main carbohydrate part, while the egg supplies protein. Checking the wrap's salt label is often more useful than worrying about the vegetables.

boiled-egg-soldiers.text: About this meal: Boiled egg and soldiers is a simple pleasure, with protein from the egg and carbohydrate from the toast. If you're watching phosphorus, remember the yolk contributes as well as the white; it doesn't mean the egg is off limits, just that the portion is worth knowing.

blueberry-cream-cheese-toast.text: About this meal: Blueberries and a little honey brighten this cream-cheese toast. It's an easy breakfast when you don't want to cook, though it isn't especially high in protein. The berries bring flavour without needing a large portion of spread, which is useful if you're comparing salt between cheese brands.

mushroom-egg-muffin.text: About this meal: Mushrooms add a lovely savoury bite to this egg muffin, while extra whites lift the protein without another yolk. There's no need for a salty breakfast meat to make it satisfying. If you're checking potassium, use the total for the complete muffin rather than judging the mushrooms alone.

strawberry-apple-french-toast.text: About this meal: Warm strawberries and apple make a naturally fruity topping for French toast. The egg-and-milk coating adds protein to what would otherwise be mostly bread and fruit. If you track potassium or phosphorus, remember the milk and fruit are part of the full serving calculation.

apple-yoghurt-toast.text: About this meal: Apple and yoghurt make a refreshing contrast with crisp toast. The yoghurt gives some protein but also contributes potassium and phosphorus. If you try a plant-based yoghurt instead, check its label: the mineral content and any added ingredients can differ quite a lot.

egg-tomato-muffin.text: About this meal: Tomato keeps the egg filling soft and fresh, and the added whites give useful protein without relying on bacon or cheese. The English muffin itself can supply a surprising amount of the salt, so compare brands if salt is on your radar.

blueberry-apple-pancakes.text: About this meal: Apple and blueberries make these pancakes feel generously topped without needing lots of syrup. The flour and syrup account for much of the carbohydrate, while the egg and milk contribute some protein. Keep the measured fruit portion in mind if you're watching potassium.

danish-bacon-egg-muffin.text: About this meal: Bacon brings plenty of savoury flavour, but it's worth checking the packet for salt and phosphate additives. The egg adds protein, so a little bacon can work as a flavour ingredient rather than the main filling. Different cured meats aren't all nutritionally alike.

jam-pancakes.text: About this meal: There's nothing wrong with enjoying simple pancakes and jam. The extra whites in the batter provide some additional protein, while the flour and jam make this a carbohydrate-rich choice. If you're counting carbohydrate, include the topping rather than just the pancakes.

egg-tomato-pepper-toast.text: About this meal: Tomato and red pepper add colour and moisture to the eggs without needing a bottled sauce. Extra whites give the filling a protein boost without another yolk. The vegetables contribute potassium, but the recorded figure reflects their measured portions in the complete breakfast.

strawberry-apple-pancakes.text: About this meal: Strawberries and apple give these pancakes a fresh, fruity topping. They also bring some fibre, which the syrup on its own wouldn't provide. If you monitor carbohydrates, remember that flour, fruit and syrup all count; there's no need to label a favourite breakfast 'good' or 'bad'.

boiled-egg-chive-cream-cheese-toast.text: About this meal: Boiled egg, chives and cream cheese make a satisfying topping with plenty of flavour. The egg supplies most of the protein; the cream cheese is there mainly for richness. If you monitor phosphorus, consider the yolk and cheese together rather than focusing on just one ingredient.

danish-bacon-tomato-toast.text: About this meal: Bacon and tomato make a familiar savoury toast, with the tomato bringing freshness. Bacon is cured, so its salt content and any phosphate additives are worth checking on the packet. You can enjoy the bacon flavour without treating a larger portion as automatically better.

egg-pepper-muffin.text: About this meal: Sweet pepper makes this egg muffin colourful and satisfying without needing cheese or processed meat. Extra egg whites contribute protein while avoiding another yolk. It's a handy example of making breakfast filling through the ingredients you cook, rather than through salty extras.

egg-white-herb-muffin.text: About this meal: Egg whites give this herb muffin protein with considerably less phosphorus from the egg than a yolk-containing version. Fresh chives add the flavour. The muffin still contributes carbohydrate and some salt, so it's worth looking at the whole breakfast rather than only the eggs.

egg-tomato-onion-wrap.text: About this meal: Soft tomato and onion make this wrap juicy enough that it doesn't need a heavy sauce. The egg contributes protein and the tortilla supplies the main carbohydrate portion. If you need to watch salt, remember the wrap and cream cheese can both contribute even before seasoning.

apple-blueberry-french-toast.text: About this meal: Apple and blueberries turn French toast into something special without requiring a lot of maple syrup. Egg and milk contribute protein, while the bread and syrup make up much of the carbohydrate. It's a lovely breakfast to enjoy with the recorded portions in mind.

three-egg-plain-omelette.text: About this meal: A plain omelette gives you a substantial portion of egg protein without cheese or cured-meat additions. Three yolks also contribute phosphorus, though, so the serving won't suit everyone's targets in the same way. Parsley provides freshness without leaning on salt.

three-egg-cheese-omelette.text: About this meal: This is a properly cheesy omelette, with protein from both the eggs and Cheddar. Those ingredients also account for its phosphorus content, so the figure is worth noticing if you monitor it. You can still enjoy a cheesy meal; the point is knowing what's in this particular serving.

three-egg-mushroom-omelette.text: About this meal: Mushrooms give this omelette a deep savoury taste without needing ham or a salty sauce. The three eggs provide plenty of protein, while the yolks contribute phosphorus and the mushrooms add potassium. The complete portion tells you more than judging any one ingredient on its own.

three-egg-ham-omelette.text: About this meal: Ham makes this omelette flavourful, but different brands can vary greatly in salt and added phosphates. The eggs provide substantial protein, so there's no need to treat the ham as the only protein source. A quick label check is useful if you make this breakfast regularly.

mixed-berry-overnight-oats.text: About this meal: Berries give overnight oats colour and a little sharpness without a big sweet topping. The oats provide fibre, while the milk contributes protein, potassium and phosphorus. Measure the milk if you have an individual fluid allowance; the recipe already includes it in the calculation.

apple-cinnamon-overnight-oats.text: About this meal: Apple and cinnamon are a lovely combination with soft overnight oats. Fibre comes from the oats and fruit, while the milk adds protein and contributes to potassium and phosphorus. It's worth considering the milk portion if you're following personalised mineral or fluid advice.

peanut-butter-greek-yoghurt-overnight-oa.text: About this meal: Peanut butter, walnuts and thick yoghurt make these oats rich and filling. They bring protein and plant fats, but also contribute to the phosphorus and potassium totals, so this isn't just a bowl of plain oats. If those nutrients are a concern, use the whole-serving figures rather than cutting out nuts by default.

blueberry-cottage-cheese-overnight-oats.text: About this meal: Cottage cheese and yoghurt give this bowl more protein than many overnight-oat breakfasts. The dairy, oats and pumpkin seeds also contribute phosphorus, and the berries bring freshness. If you're comparing brands, watch for changes in salt or added ingredients, especially in cottage cheese.

cornflakes-and-milk.text: About this meal: Cornflakes and milk make a quick, familiar breakfast. The milk contributes most of the protein here and counts towards a fluid allowance if you've been given one. Cereal brands can differ in salt and fortification, so the packet is useful when you want the closest match to the recorded values.

weetabix-and-milk.text: About this meal: Weetabix brings wholegrain fibre alongside the milk's protein. It's straightforward and easy to measure, which can help when you keep track of your intake. The milk also supplies potassium and phosphorus and may count towards a fluid limit if you have one.

warm-blueberry-and-walnut-rice-porridge.text: About this meal: Blueberries, cinnamon and walnuts make this rice porridge feel special, with a little crunch against the soft grains. The walnuts bring plant fats and some phosphorus, while the oats add fibre. There isn't much protein here, so bear that in mind if you're aiming for a higher-protein breakfast.

blueberry-oat-and-tofu-pancakes.text: About this meal: Tofu helps make these blueberry pancakes more satisfying than a flour-only version, and oats contribute fibre. The tofu specified is a plain, calcium-set variety; flavoured or marinated versions may change the salt content. A squeeze of lemon brightens the berries without needing extra sugar.

seitan-pepper-and-breakfast-rice-hash.text: About this meal: Seitan provides a concentrated source of wheat protein, while rice, boiled potato and peppers make this feel like a hearty breakfast hash. The potato has been boiled and drained before use; that preparation matters if you're following potassium advice. Use vital wheat gluten for the seitan rather than ordinary flour.

spiced-tofu-scramble-with-rice-flatbread.text: About this meal: Cumin and turmeric give this tofu scramble plenty of warmth without relying on a salty sauce. Spinach and tomato add colour, while the rice flatbread makes it a complete breakfast. Tofu contributes protein, and the measured greens are included in the potassium figure.

white-bean-and-basil-breakfast-polenta.text: About this meal: Creamy polenta, beans and basil make a comforting savoury breakfast with fibre from the beans and vegetables. The walnuts add crunch and plant fats. Beans and tomato contribute potassium, so take the full serving into account if that's a nutrient you're managing, rather than avoiding pulses altogether.

lentil-and-groundnut-breakfast-fritters.text: About this meal: These lentil fritters have real substance from the pulses, with cabbage, carrot and coriander keeping them fresh. The peanuts add crunch and some plant protein. Lentils contain phosphorus, but plant phosphorus is generally absorbed differently from phosphate additives in highly processed foods.

seitan-and-white-bean-breakfast-wrap.text: About this meal: Seitan and white beans give this wrap a substantial protein-and-fibre filling, while lemon and parsley keep it bright. It's a useful plant-based option, though the beans and wheat protein still contribute minerals. If you monitor potassium, check the whole wrap rather than judging the beans alone.

feta-and-spinach-breakfast-omelette.text: About this meal: Salty feta brings plenty of character to this spinach omelette, so there's little need for extra seasoning. The egg and additional whites provide protein. Feta also contributes salt and phosphorus, so its measured portion matters if either is part of your dietary advice.

salmon-and-egg-breakfast-cup.text: About this meal: Salmon and egg make this little breakfast cup rich in protein, and salmon provides beneficial omega-3 fats. Both ingredients contribute phosphorus, so the serving is worth checking if you monitor it. As there's no fruit, vegetable or grain here, you may want fibre elsewhere in the day.

bean-and-seitan-brunch-rice-bowl.text: About this meal: This is a hearty brunch bowl, with protein from seitan and beans, fibre from brown rice and pulses, and freshness from pepper and lemon. It provides a substantial amount of food and protein in one serving, which may be useful for some people and more than others need. Check its potassium and phosphorus figures alongside your personal targets.

chicken-lettuce-sandwich.text: About this meal: A simple chicken sandwich can be a useful protein-rich lunch without needing a processed-meat filling. Crisp lettuce and a measured amount of mayonnaise keep it fresh and creamy. If salt is part of your dietary advice, compare bread and mayonnaise labels; those choices can matter more than the lettuce.

egg-lettuce-sandwich.text: About this meal: Egg and lettuce is a comforting classic, with the eggs providing most of the protein. The yolks also contribute phosphorus, so the number of eggs matters if you're monitoring it. The crisp lettuce adds freshness without needing more mayonnaise.

tuna-lettuce-sandwich.text: About this meal: Tuna makes a quick, protein-containing filling, and lettuce adds crunch. Because this tuna is canned in brine, drain it well and check the tin for salt; brands can vary. Choosing a different tuna product may change the nutrition from the figures shown here.

chicken-cucumber-sandwich.text: About this meal: Chicken and cucumber make a fresh, satisfying lunch, with protein from the chicken and crunch from the cucumber. Bread and mayonnaise are worth checking for salt if you're managing it. There's no need to add a salty sauce to make this sandwich enjoyable.

egg-mayo-sandwich.text: About this meal: Chives brighten this creamy egg sandwich without needing a heavy seasoning. The eggs provide useful protein and also contain phosphorus, especially in the yolks. If you make egg mayonnaise often, comparing bread and mayonnaise labels is a practical way to keep an eye on salt.

chicken-red-pepper-sandwich.text: About this meal: Sweet red pepper lifts this chicken sandwich with colour and crunch. Chicken gives it a useful amount of protein, while the measured mayonnaise keeps the filling creamy. If you're watching salt, check the bread and spread rather than assuming the fresh ingredients are the problem.

ham-lettuce-sandwich.text: About this meal: Chives and lettuce make a familiar egg sandwich taste fresh rather than heavy. The eggs contribute protein as well as phosphorus; the bread and mayonnaise also affect the overall salt figure. Enjoy the combination and use the whole-serving numbers when making your choices.

chicken-cream-cheese-sandwich.text: About this meal: Cream cheese and cucumber give this chicken sandwich a lovely balance of creamy and crisp. The chicken supplies most of the protein; the cheese is mainly there for texture and flavour. Compare cream-cheese labels for salt if you have a specific limit.

chicken-lettuce-wrap.text: About this meal: A chicken and lettuce wrap is a handy lunch with protein and plenty of crunch. Tortilla wraps can contain more salt than you expect, so check the packet if you're monitoring sodium. The measured mayonnaise is part of the recorded nutrition too.

tuna-mayo-wrap.text: About this meal: Tuna mayo works just as well in a wrap, and the lettuce keeps it fresh. Drain brined tuna before mixing; it helps with texture, although the product's own salt level still matters. With protein from the fish and carbohydrate from the wrap, this is more than just a quick snack.

egg-chive-wrap.text: About this meal: Egg and chive makes a gentle, savoury filling that doesn't need a salty sauce for flavour. The eggs provide protein and phosphorus, while the tortilla adds carbohydrate and some salt. It's worth comparing tortilla brands if you enjoy wraps regularly.

chicken-cucumber-wrap.text: About this meal: Cool cucumber makes a nice contrast to the warm chicken in this wrap. The chicken provides protein, while the tortilla and mayonnaise shape the carbohydrate and salt totals. A fresh filling can be just as satisfying without relying on cured meat or cheese.

chicken-pepper-pasta.text: About this meal: Chicken, pepper and onion give this pasta plenty of substance without needing a creamy sauce. Pasta supplies energy and carbohydrate, while chicken contributes protein and phosphorus. The colourful vegetables add flavour and variety; their measured portions are already included in the potassium figure.

creamy-chicken-pasta.text: About this meal: Cream cheese softens this chicken pasta into an easy comfort meal. The chicken contributes protein and phosphorus, while the cheese brings creaminess along with some salt. Keep the measured cheese portion in mind if you're comparing this dish with a different sauce.

tuna-pepper-pasta.text: About this meal: Tuna, red pepper and chives make a bright pasta lunch with protein and plenty of texture. Drain the brined tuna well, and check its salt content against other brands. The mayonnaise binds the dish without needing an extra bottled dressing.

egg-cream-cheese-pasta.text: About this meal: Egg and cream cheese turn simple pasta into something comforting and filling. Both ingredients contribute protein, but also phosphorus, so the serving is worth a look if that's a nutrient you monitor. Fresh chives give the creamy sauce a lift without adding another salty topping.

chicken-onion-pasta.text: About this meal: Onion brings sweetness to this creamy chicken pasta, while the chicken does most of the work on protein. Cream cheese can vary in salt between brands, so it's worth checking the label if you make this regularly. The pasta provides a satisfying carbohydrate portion alongside the filling.

chicken-mushroom-pasta.text: About this meal: Mushrooms add a lovely savoury depth to chicken and cream-cheese pasta. The chicken provides protein, while mushrooms and cheese also contribute to the potassium and phosphorus totals. If you monitor either nutrient, look at the whole serving rather than singling out mushrooms as something to avoid.

tuna-cream-cheese-pasta.text: About this meal: Tuna and cream cheese make a smooth, protein-containing pasta sauce without much fuss. Brined tuna and cheese can both contribute salt, so the product labels are worth checking. Chives bring a fresh finish without needing an additional salty sauce.

chicken-fried-rice.text: About this meal: Chicken and egg make this fried rice a satisfying protein-rich lunch. Pepper and onion keep it colourful, and cooking the rice at home lets you use a measured amount of oil rather than a ready-made sauce. The egg and chicken both contribute phosphorus, so check the full serving if you're monitoring it.

tuna-egg-rice-bowl.text: About this meal: Tuna and egg make this rice bowl particularly rich in protein. They also contribute phosphorus, so it's worth looking at that total if you're monitoring it. Cool cucumber and a little mayonnaise balance the filling without needing a heavily seasoned dressing.

chicken-jacket-potato.text: Potassium: Jacket potatoes are wonderfully filling, but this serving has a substantial potassium contribution from the potato. If you've been advised to limit potassium, it's worth checking the total rather than assuming a small chicken topping makes the whole lunch low in it. The chicken adds useful protein.

tuna-jacket-potato.text: Potassium: This jacket potato delivers a fairly substantial potassium portion, even though tuna and mayonnaise are familiar, simple toppings. That's mainly a reason to look at the recorded total if you manage potassium, not a reason to ban potatoes outright. The tuna supplies protein; drain it well if it's canned in brine.

egg-mayo-jacket-potato.text: Potassium: A jacket potato with egg mayo is comforting, and the egg adds protein. The potato accounts for a significant part of this meal's potassium, while the egg yolk contributes phosphorus. If you're monitoring either, the whole-serving figures help you fit a favourite lunch into your own advice.

chicken-potato-hash.text: Potassium: This chicken hash gets much of its body from potatoes, which make a substantial contribution to the potassium total. The chicken adds protein and the pepper and onion bring flavour without a salty sauce. If you need a lower-potassium preparation, ask your dietitian whether boiling and draining potatoes would suit your plan; that would change the recipe's calculations.

egg-potato-hash.text: Potassium: Crisp potato, soft egg and sweet pepper make a satisfying hash, but the potatoes mean this isn't a particularly low-potassium lunch. If potassium matters for you, use the recorded figure rather than trying to judge it by the amount of egg. The egg also adds protein and phosphorus.

tuna-potato-salad.text: Potassium: Potato salad can still be part of a varied menu, but this portion contains a substantial amount of potassium. Tuna provides protein and the cucumber and lettuce bring freshness. If you're watching salt too, check the drained tuna and mayonnaise labels rather than focusing only on the potato.

chicken-pepper-omelette.text: About this meal: Chicken and egg make this pepper omelette substantial in protein. They also both contribute phosphorus, while the peppers and onion provide colour and flavour without a salty sauce. It's a satisfying lunch with a clear nutritional profile to compare with your own advice.

mushroom-chive-omelette.text: About this meal: Mushrooms and chives give this omelette a savoury lift, while the toast makes it more filling. The eggs supply protein and phosphorus; mushrooms also contribute potassium. There's no need to avoid the vegetable automatically—look at the full portion if you're monitoring potassium.

egg-pepper-toast.text: About this meal: Egg and sweet pepper make a simple toast topping with useful protein and colour. The bread contributes carbohydrate and salt, so it's worth comparing loaves if you're managing sodium. The pepper adds flavour without needing a processed-meat topping.

chicken-pepper-toastie.text: About this meal: Warm chicken, red pepper and a little cream cheese make a comforting toastie. Chicken provides protein; the bread and cheese can both contribute salt. Check their labels if needed, and let the pepper bring sweetness rather than reaching for another sauce.

tuna-cucumber-toastie.text: About this meal: Tuna and cucumber are a lovely combination in a warm toastie, with a creamy mayonnaise filling. Brined tuna needs draining and may still contain salt, so compare brands. The cucumber adds freshness rather than making the filling heavier.

chicken-apple-sandwich.text: About this meal: Apple gives this chicken sandwich an unexpectedly good crunch and a hint of sweetness. The chicken makes it protein-rich, while lettuce and apple keep the filling fresh. Bread and mayonnaise are the practical places to look if you're trying to manage salt.

egg-cucumber-sandwich.text: About this meal: Egg and cucumber make a classic, cooling sandwich, with protein from the eggs and crunch from the cucumber. The yolks contribute phosphorus, so keep the two-egg portion in mind if that's part of your dietary advice. A little mayonnaise is enough to bring the filling together.

chicken-cream-cheese-wrap.text: About this meal: Chicken, cucumber and lettuce make a crisp wrap, softened by a little cream cheese. The chicken supplies most of the protein. Wraps and spreads can differ in salt, so their labels are useful if you're watching sodium—even when the filling is freshly made.

tuna-cream-cheese-wrap.text: About this meal: Tuna and cream cheese give this wrap a creamy, protein-containing filling, while cucumber makes it lighter to eat. Drain brined tuna properly, and compare the fish and cheese labels if salt is a concern. There's no need for a salty dressing on top.

chicken-onion-pasta-salad.text: About this meal: Chicken and pasta make a satisfying lunch, with crunchy cucumber to balance the softer ingredients. Onion adds natural savoury sweetness. The pasta provides carbohydrate and the chicken provides protein; the mayonnaise can vary in salt depending on the brand.

chicken-leek-couscous-bowl.text: About this meal: Lemon and parsley brighten the chicken, couscous and leeks without relying on a stock cube. The chicken brings protein, while couscous provides an easy carbohydrate base. The carrots and leeks add vegetables without making the dish feel like a 'diet' meal.

turkey-cucumber-pitta.text: About this meal: Turkey and cucumber are a fresh, protein-rich filling for a soft pitta. The lettuce adds crunch, and parsley gives flavour without needing a salty sauce. If salt matters for you, check the pitta and mayonnaise labels—they can vary more than the fresh vegetables.

tuna-sweetcorn-pasta-salad.text: About this meal: Sweetcorn and cucumber give tuna pasta salad plenty of texture and colour. Tuna supplies protein, and the pasta is the main carbohydrate portion. Since the tuna is packed in brine, draining it and checking the label are sensible steps if you're managing salt.

chicken-carrot-noodle-salad.text: About this meal: Ginger and lemon lift this chicken noodle salad, so it doesn't need a salty bottled dressing. Chicken provides protein, and the rice noodles offer a light-textured carbohydrate base. Carrot and cucumber bring colour and crunch; their measured portions are included in the potassium total.

turkey-apple-couscous-salad.text: About this meal: Apple makes a lovely sweet-sharp contrast with turkey and couscous, while cucumber and parsley keep it fresh. Turkey supplies protein and phosphorus, and the couscous provides carbohydrate. It's a useful lunch for anyone who enjoys variety without relying on heavy sauces.

cod-cucumber-pasta-salad.text: About this meal: Lemon and parsley keep this cod pasta salad bright, with cucumber and lettuce providing crunch. Cod gives the dish a substantial protein portion and also contributes phosphorus. If you're watching potassium, use the meal's recorded figure rather than assuming the salad vegetables are the main issue.

chicken-leek-toasted-pitta.text: About this meal: Chicken and softened leeks make a comforting warm pitta filling. Chives add flavour, so there's little need for a salty sauce beyond the measured mayonnaise. The chicken provides protein, while the pitta and mayonnaise are worth checking for salt if that's one of your targets.

chicken-tikka-naan-style-flatbread.text: About this meal: Yoghurt, lemon and warm spices give the chicken plenty of flavour without depending on a shop-bought tikka sauce. The freshly made flatbread makes this a substantial meal, and the chicken contributes protein and phosphorus. With more than 1,000 mg of potassium recorded, it's worth considering the whole serving if you monitor potassium.

spiced-turkey-keema-stuffed-pitta.text: About this meal: Turkey keema is full of flavour from ginger, cumin and coriander, with yoghurt and cucumber cooling things down. The turkey makes it protein-rich, and the pitta provides the carbohydrate. Peas and tomato contribute potassium, so the recorded serving is worth considering if your advice includes a potassium limit.

bombay-style-cauliflower-and-egg-rolls.text: About this meal: Cauliflower, onion and egg make a gently spiced filling for these homemade rolls. Lemon and coriander brighten the flavour without needing a bottled sauce. The egg provides protein, while the flour wrappers account for much of the carbohydrate—useful to know if you're tracking it.

coconut-chicken-hopper-style-bowl.text: About this meal: Coconut milk gives this hopper-style bowl its lovely richness, while curry leaves and spices bring character. Chicken provides protein, and the rice-flour hopper adds carbohydrate. This is a substantial serving with a high recorded potassium figure, so it's worth checking against personal advice if you monitor potassium.

chicken-shawarma-with-garlic-flatbread.text: About this meal: Garlic, lemon and warm shawarma spices make the chicken and flatbread wonderfully flavourful without a bottled dressing. Chicken provides plenty of protein, while the bread supplies energy. The recorded potassium is just over 1,000 mg, so anyone monitoring potassium should look at the whole serving rather than assuming the meal is automatically low or off limits.

lamb-kofta-with-herbed-bulgur.text: About this meal: Fragrant lamb kofta and lemony bulgur make a satisfying combination. The lamb brings protein and phosphorus, while bulgur and herbs add variety and some fibre. This is a substantial portion of potassium and phosphorus, so the numbers are worth checking if you're managing either nutrient.

lemon-chicken-souvlaki-with-warm-pitta.text: About this meal: Lemon, oregano and garlic give the chicken plenty of Greek-inspired flavour, and yoghurt and cucumber make a cooling accompaniment. This is a high-protein meal, which may suit some dialysis plans but not everyone's needs. It also has a substantial recorded potassium content, so the whole-serving figures matter.

chermoula-fish-with-couscous.text: About this meal: Chermoula brings cod to life with coriander, parsley, lemon and spices, without needing a bottled sauce. Cod supplies protein and phosphorus, and couscous makes a satisfying base. The potassium figure reflects the entire meal, including the carrot; use it if you're following personalised potassium advice.

spiced-egg-and-pepper-shakshuka-with-bre.text: About this meal: Shakshuka is a delicious way to enjoy eggs with a richly spiced pepper-and-tomato sauce. The bread makes it a complete meal, while cumin and paprika provide flavour without needing a salty ready-made sauce. Tomato-based dishes can contain a meaningful amount of potassium, and this serving's total is worth noting if you monitor it.

pork-and-ginger-steamed-dumplings.text: About this meal: Ginger and Chinese cabbage make these pork dumplings fragrant, with the dipping sauce adding a savoury finish. Soy sauce contributes salt, so the measured amount matters; some reduced-salt products contain potassium-based substitutes. The pork provides protein, and the homemade wrappers supply carbohydrate.

chicken-katsu-with-rice-and-cabbage-slaw.text: About this meal: Crisp chicken katsu with rice and cabbage is a satisfying meal, with protein from the chicken and carbohydrate from the rice and coating. The homemade sauce includes soy, so it contributes salt even if you don't season the slaw. This is a generous portion; its potassium and phosphorus figures deserve a look if you monitor them.

bulgogi-style-beef-lettuce-cups.text: About this meal: Pear, ginger and sesame give the beef a lovely sweet-savoury flavour. Lettuce and cucumber add crunch, while rice makes it filling. Soy sauce is an important source of salt here, so use the amount in the recipe and check the brand if you're managing sodium.

lemongrass-chicken-noodle-salad.text: About this meal: Lemongrass, mint and lime make this chicken noodle salad really fresh and lively. Fish sauce brings a distinctive savoury note but also salt, so the measured dressing matters. Chicken provides protein, while noodles and crunchy vegetables give a satisfying mix of textures.

banh-mi-inspired-chicken-baguette.text: About this meal: Pickled carrot and mooli give this chicken baguette its lovely tang, with coriander and chilli doing plenty of the flavouring. Soy and fish sauce in the marinade contribute salt, as does the bread. The chicken supplies protein, and the crunchy vegetables keep it fresh without extra dressing.

chicken-satay-style-rice-noodle-salad.text: About this meal: Lime, tamarind and peanuts make this satay-style noodle salad full of flavour. Peanuts contribute plant fat and phosphorus, while the chicken supplies substantial protein. The soy sauce adds salt, and the recorded phosphorus is worth considering if you're keeping track of it.

chicken-and-pepper-quesadillas.text: About this meal: Warm cumin-spiced chicken and peppers make these quesadillas wonderfully satisfying. Cheddar adds richness and protein, but also phosphorus and salt alongside the chicken. This serving contains a substantial amount of both protein and phosphorus, so it's one to judge against your individual needs rather than a generic 'good' or 'bad' label.

soft-fish-tacos-with-lime-slaw.text: About this meal: Lime, coriander and crunchy cabbage bring freshness to these soft fish tacos. Cod supplies protein, and the yoghurt slaw adds creaminess without a heavy bottled sauce. The recorded phosphorus and potassium are relatively substantial, so the whole-serving figures are useful if your kidney team has advised monitoring them.

jerk-chicken-flatbread.text: About this meal: Allspice, thyme, ginger and lime give jerk-style chicken its lively flavour, while cucumber and cabbage bring cooling crunch. The chicken provides protein and the flatbread makes this a substantial lunch. Bright herbs and fresh vegetables do plenty of work here without a bottled sauce.

suya-spiced-chicken-skewers-with-flatbre.text: About this meal: The peanut-and-spice coating gives these suya-inspired chicken skewers loads of flavour, with tomato and lime adding freshness. Peanuts and chicken both contribute phosphorus, and the flatbread provides carbohydrate. If you're monitoring phosphorus, it's worth considering the coating alongside the chicken.

mildly-spiced-chicken-kelewele-inspired-.text: About this meal: Sweet plantain and warm ginger make this kelewele-inspired bowl a real treat alongside savoury chicken. Plantain can contribute a substantial amount of potassium, so the portion matters if you monitor it. Chilli, lime and coriander brighten the dish without a ready-made sauce.

white-bean-and-roasted-pepper-bruschetta.text: About this meal: Creamy white beans, roast peppers and garlic make a lovely topping for crisp bread. The beans bring fibre and plant protein, while walnuts add crunch and healthy fats. If you're managing potassium or phosphorus, use the full serving totals rather than avoiding beans automatically.

courgette-and-ricotta-bake-with-garlic-t.text: About this meal: Ricotta keeps this courgette bake soft, and garlic toast makes it a satisfying lunch. Egg white adds some protein without another yolk, while walnuts bring texture and plant fats. If phosphorus is on your radar, consider the ricotta and walnuts together; neither needs to be ruled out automatically.

basil-and-walnut-pasta-salad-with-ricott.text: About this meal: Basil, walnuts and lemon make this pasta salad taste bright and fresh, with ricotta adding creaminess. Nuts and cheese both contribute phosphorus, although phosphorus in plant foods isn't absorbed in quite the same way as phosphate additives. The portions are already counted in the figures, so you can enjoy the combination with that information in mind.

white-bean-and-cumin-patties-with-lemon-.text: About this meal: White beans give these cumin patties a soft middle and plenty of fibre, while the lemony cabbage slaw keeps everything lively. Beans also contribute potassium and phosphorus, so the recorded totals are useful if you're monitoring those nutrients. Fresh herbs mean the slaw doesn't need a salty dressing.

chickpea-and-carrot-flatbread-with-walnu.text: About this meal: Chickpeas and carrot make a hearty flatbread filling, with lemon and walnut dressing bringing richness and crunch. The chickpeas provide fibre and plant protein, while the walnuts add phosphorus and healthy fats. It's a good example of enjoying pulses in measured portions rather than automatically excluding them from kidney-friendly eating.

egg-and-mustard-pasta-salad.text: About this meal: Mustard seeds, chives and lemon give this egg pasta salad a lovely sharpness. The extra egg whites increase protein without needing more yolks, which can be helpful when phosphorus also matters. Pasta makes this a carbohydrate-containing lunch, so include it when tracking your intake.

pepper-and-herb-frittata-with-toasted-br.text: About this meal: Soft mozzarella and sweet pepper turn this frittata into a satisfying lunch, with crusty bread alongside. The whole egg and extra whites provide protein, while the cheese contributes salt and phosphorus. Basil gives it flavour without needing a salty bottled dressing.

black-bean-and-sweetcorn-cakes-with-lime.text: About this meal: Black beans and sweetcorn make these crisp cakes hearty, with lime and cabbage keeping the slaw fresh. Beans bring fibre and plant protein as well as potassium. If you monitor potassium, use the value for the complete meal rather than assuming black beans can never be included.

buckwheat-galette-with-mushrooms-and-wal.text: About this meal: This buckwheat galette has a lovely savoury filling of mushrooms, leek and ricotta, with walnuts for crunch. The cheese and nuts contribute phosphorus, while mushrooms add potassium. The complete serving is the useful figure if either mineral is part of your dietary advice.

chickpea-and-egg-salad-with-crisp-crouto.text: About this meal: Chickpeas, egg and crisp croutons turn a salad into a satisfying lunch. The chickpeas bring fibre and plant protein, while the egg provides more concentrated protein and some phosphorus. Lemon and parsley do the flavouring without needing a heavy ready-made dressing.

potato-and-chive-cakes-with-herb-mayonna.text: About this meal: Crisp potato-and-chive cakes are lovely with cool cucumber and herb mayonnaise. The potato has been boiled and drained before use, which matters to the potassium calculation. If you're following potassium advice, don't assume the same numbers apply to raw potato cooked a different way.

cabbage-mushroom-and-white-bean-pierogi.text: About this meal: Cabbage, mushrooms and white beans make a comforting pierogi filling, with a little ricotta for richness. Beans bring fibre, and the cheese contributes protein and phosphorus. It's a satisfying meat-free choice; the recorded mineral values cover the filling and dough together.

carrot-and-coriander-soup-with-toast.text: About this meal: Carrot and coriander soup is warming without needing a salty stock cube, and the toast makes it a more substantial lunch. The yoghurt adds a creamy finish. If you record fluid, remember soup counts according to the guidance you've been given; the water used in this bowl is part of what you're eating.

creamy-mushroom-spaghetti-with-walnuts.text: About this meal: Mushrooms, parsley and lemon keep this creamy spaghetti full of savoury flavour, while walnuts add crunch. Yoghurt makes the sauce creamy, with protein and phosphorus alongside it. This isn't a particularly high-protein pasta dish, so that may be worth considering if your treatment plan calls for more protein.

crisp-rice-pancakes-with-cabbage-and-pea.text: About this meal: Crisp rice pancakes are a lovely contrast to soft chickpeas, cabbage and a zingy peanut dressing. The chickpeas bring fibre, and peanuts add plant fats and some phosphorus. Lime and ginger give plenty of flavour without making soy sauce the centre of the dressing.

chickpea-chaat-with-herbed-yoghurt-dress.text: About this meal: Chickpea chaat is all about contrast: soft potato, crunchy cucumber, bright herbs and cooling yoghurt. Both chickpeas and potatoes contribute potassium, but they're included here in measured portions. If you track potassium, look at the full serving figure rather than trying to avoid every individual ingredient.

coconut-roti-with-spiced-cabbage.text: About this meal: Coconut roti and gently spiced cabbage make a lovely simple lunch, with mustard seeds and lime adding character. The coconut and oil provide much of the energy, while the dish is relatively light on protein. That's useful to know if you're planning a higher-protein day rather than simply assuming every main meal will provide it.

vegetable-and-lentil-khichuri.text: About this meal: Rice and red lentils cook into a comforting khichuri, with ginger, turmeric and vegetables bringing warmth. Lentils contribute fibre and plant protein, plus potassium and phosphorus. If you're monitoring minerals, the figures reflect the whole bowl; pulses don't automatically have to disappear from the menu.

salmon-and-cucumber-rice-salad.text: About this meal: Salmon brings protein and omega-3 fats to this cool rice salad, while cucumber and lemon keep it fresh. Sesame seeds add a little crunch and phosphorus. It's a satisfying lunch with a measured portion of fish, so the mineral figures are more useful than a blanket rule about salmon.

tofu-cabbage-and-ginger-pancakes.text: About this meal: Ginger, cabbage and tofu make these pancakes savoury and satisfying, with lime lifting the flavour. The tofu specified is plain and calcium-set; smoked or marinated versions may have more salt. Soy sauce also adds salt, so the measured amount matters if you're managing sodium.

steamed-cabbage-mushroom-and-white-bean-.text: About this meal: These steamed buns are filled with soft beans, cabbage and mushrooms, with ginger giving them warmth. Beans supply fibre and plant protein, while soy sauce adds the savoury note and some salt. If you use a reduced-salt sauce, check whether it contains potassium-based substitutes.

chicken-lettuce-cups-with-ginger-and-pea.text: About this meal: Crisp lettuce and cucumber make a fresh contrast with warm ginger chicken and peanut dressing. The chicken supplies protein, and peanuts add plant fats and phosphorus. Soy sauce can make even a homemade dressing salty, so its measured portion is worth keeping in mind.

vegetable-and-tofu-popiah-rolls.text: About this meal: These popiah-style rolls have a lovely mix of tender tofu, crunchy vegetables and peanuts. Tofu and egg white provide protein, while peanuts add texture and phosphorus. The soy-based seasoning contains salt, so measuring it is worthwhile if that's one of your targets.

gado-gado-with-peanut-and-coconut-dressi.text: About this meal: Gado-gado is a wonderful mix of soft egg, vegetables and a rich peanut-coconut dressing. The potatoes are already boiled and drained, which matters when estimating potassium. Soy sauce brings salt to the dressing; the measured amount is part of the recorded total.

black-bean-tostadas-with-avocado-and-lim.text: About this meal: Black beans, sweetcorn and lime make these tostadas lively, with avocado adding creaminess. Beans bring fibre and plant protein, while avocado contributes potassium. There's room for variety in kidney-friendly food; the key is knowing the portion and the total if potassium is something you monitor.

tuna-and-lime-potato-causa.text: About this meal: Lime gives this Peruvian-inspired potato causa a bright finish, with tuna adding protein and cucumber providing crunch. The potatoes are boiled and drained before assembly, a detail that matters for potassium estimates. Brined tuna may also contribute salt, so check the tin if you're managing sodium.

black-beans-and-rice-with-lime-dressed-c.text: About this meal: Black beans and rice are a satisfying combination, with cabbage and lime keeping the bowl fresh. Beans contribute fibre and plant protein as well as potassium and phosphorus. The recorded values let you enjoy pulses thoughtfully without treating them as automatically off limits.

plantain-and-black-eyed-pea-fritters-wit.text: About this meal: Sweet plantain and earthy black-eyed peas make these fritters hearty, with peanuts adding crunch. Plantain and pulses both contribute potassium, so this isn't a dish to assume is low in it. Lime and ginger give plenty of flavour without relying on a salty sauce.

black-eyed-pea-and-tomato-stew-with-soft.text: About this meal: Soft polenta is lovely with a warmly spiced black-eyed pea and tomato stew. The peas provide fibre and plant protein, while ginger, paprika and garlic bring flavour. Tomato and pulses contribute potassium, so look at the full-bowl figure if that's part of your dietary advice.

lentil-and-groundnut-stew-with-flatbread.text: About this meal: Lentils and peanuts give this stew body and a lovely nutty flavour, with flatbread making it a filling lunch. The lentils supply fibre and plant protein. Both lentils and peanuts contain phosphorus, but naturally occurring plant phosphorus is not absorbed in the same way as phosphate additives.

pea-and-mint-soup-with-toast.text: About this meal: Mint and lemon make this pea soup fresh and comforting, with toast adding substance. Peas offer fibre and some protein, while yoghurt gives a creamy finish. If you have an individual fluid allowance, remember the soup itself can contribute; follow the method your renal team has given you for counting it.

salmon-avocado-and-cucumber-salad.text: About this meal: Salmon, avocado and cucumber make a fresh salad with protein and plenty of healthy fats. Avocado is also a significant potassium-containing ingredient, so this meal is worth checking against your own guidance if you monitor potassium. Lemon and chives bring flavour without needing a bottled dressing.

chicken-and-avocado-lettuce-wraps.text: About this meal: Chicken and avocado make these lettuce wraps satisfying without bread, with cucumber and lime adding freshness. The chicken supplies protein, while avocado contributes potassium and healthy fats. If you're monitoring potassium, the portion matters more than treating avocado as automatically forbidden.

spinach-egg-and-mozzarella-skillet.text: About this meal: Soft mozzarella, spinach and egg make a lovely one-pan lunch. The egg and extra whites provide protein, while the cheese contributes phosphorus and salt. Spinach also contributes potassium; the meal's recorded figures account for the measured amount rather than a huge serving of greens.

tuna-egg-and-cucumber-boats.text: About this meal: Tuna and egg make these cool cucumber boats surprisingly filling, with plenty of protein and almost no preparation fuss. Both contribute phosphorus, and brined tuna may contain added salt. A squeeze of lemon and some chives give a fresher finish than another spoonful of dressing.

beef-and-cheddar-lettuce-cups.text: About this meal: Beef and Cheddar make these lettuce cups rich in protein, with cucumber adding a welcome crunch. The cheese brings phosphorus and salt as well as flavour. Because there's no starchy accompaniment, the meal may suit some carbohydrate preferences better than others; it isn't a universal recommendation.

salmon-with-softly-set-egg.text: About this meal: Salmon and softly set egg make a rich, protein-forward meal with very little carbohydrate. They also both provide phosphorus. There's no fruit, vegetable or wholegrain accompaniment in this recipe, so you may want to enjoy some fibre-rich foods elsewhere in the day if they fit your advice.

sirloin-steak-with-a-baked-egg.text: About this meal: Steak and egg make a hearty, protein-rich pairing, though both also contribute phosphorus. With no vegetables or grains in the recipe, it offers little fibre. A balanced diet is about the whole day, so you can enjoy a simple plate like this while making room for variety elsewhere.

pork-medallions-with-scrambled-eggs.text: About this meal: Pork medallions and scrambled eggs provide a generous amount of protein in a small plate. They also contribute phosphorus, which is worth noting if you're managing it. There's no vegetable or grain included, so this isn't intended to be your only source of dietary variety.

chicken-and-egg-mini-patties.text: About this meal: These little chicken-and-egg patties make a simple, protein-rich lunch. The meat and eggs also contribute phosphorus. Because the recipe contains no vegetables or grains, consider whether the rest of your food that day provides the fibre and variety you enjoy.

tuna-and-cucumber-rice-salad.text: About this meal: Lemon and parsley keep this tuna rice salad fresh, with cucumber and carrot bringing crunch. Tuna provides protein, and rice makes it a substantial lunch. Drain the brined fish and check the label for salt if you're managing it.

chive-and-spinach-rice-pancakes.text: About this meal: Chives and spinach make these rice pancakes fresh and savoury. The whole egg and extra whites provide protein without needing a cheese-heavy filling, while rice flour provides carbohydrate. Spinach contributes potassium, but the measured amount is already included in the meal's figures.

chive-omelette-with-soft-polenta-and-car.text: About this meal: A fluffy chive omelette with soft polenta makes a comforting lunch, and carrots bring a bit of colour. Extra egg whites increase the protein without another yolk, while the polenta provides carbohydrate. The egg yolk still contributes phosphorus, so the complete serving is the useful measure.

white-bean-and-brown-rice-salad.text: About this meal: White beans and brown rice make this salad satisfying, with cucumber, pepper and lemon keeping it fresh. Both the beans and wholegrains bring fibre, and walnuts add a little crunch. Plant foods contain potassium and phosphorus too, so use the whole-serving figures if you monitor them.

lemon-chickpea-and-quinoa-bowl.text: About this meal: Chickpeas, quinoa and crunchy vegetables make a lively bowl with fibre and plant protein. Walnuts contribute texture and plant fats. The potassium amount is relatively substantial, so this is one to look at in context if you manage potassium rather than automatically avoiding the chickpeas.

oat-and-carrot-pancakes-with-white-beans.text: About this meal: Oats and white beans make these carrot pancakes surprisingly hearty, while chives and lemon provide freshness. Beans bring fibre and plant protein, and the egg whites add more protein with little phosphorus from the egg. It's a nice example of using everyday ingredients in a different way.

lentil-and-barley-herb-salad.text: About this meal: Lentils and barley give this salad plenty of fibre, with lemon, parsley and crunchy vegetables keeping it lively. Walnuts add richness and plant fats. Pulses and wholegrains contribute phosphorus, but that's different from the highly absorbable phosphate additives found in some processed foods.

ginger-tofu-and-brown-rice-bowl.text: About this meal: Ginger and coriander lift this tofu-and-rice bowl, with cabbage and carrot giving it crunch. Plain tofu supplies plant protein, and brown rice adds fibre. The soy sauce contributes salt; check the label if using a reduced-salt version, as some contain potassium substitutes.

white-bean-walnut-pasta-with-frittata-ri.text: About this meal: White beans, walnuts and ribbons of egg-white frittata make this pasta more substantial than a plain vegetable sauce. The beans bring fibre and the egg whites add protein, while walnuts contribute plant fats and phosphorus. The recorded potassium total is worth considering if you monitor it.

chicken-groundnut-and-black-eyed-pea-ric.text: About this meal: Chicken, black-eyed peas and peanuts make this a hearty rice bowl with protein and fibre. The peanuts add nutty flavour, and ginger and paprika keep the dish lively without a bottled sauce. The complete serving has meaningful potassium and phosphorus amounts, so check it against your own advice if you monitor either.

lime-fish-and-avocado-rice-bowl.text: About this meal: Lime and coriander brighten the cod, avocado and rice, with cabbage adding crunch. Cod provides protein, while avocado contributes potassium and healthy fats. If you've been given potassium guidance, the recorded total matters more than treating avocado as universally unsuitable.

potato-and-herb-cakes-with-egg-salad.text: About this meal: Crispy potato-and-herb cakes are lovely beside a cool egg salad. The potatoes have been boiled and drained before use, which matters when estimating their potassium. Egg and extra whites add protein, while chives and lemon keep the dressing lively without needing a salty sauce.

ginger-tofu-and-peanut-noodle-salad.text: About this meal: Ginger, lime and peanuts make this tofu noodle salad full of character. Tofu supplies plant protein, peanuts add phosphorus and crunch, and soy sauce contributes salt. The measured dressing is part of the recorded nutrition, so a different bottled sauce could change the figures.

lemon-herb-chicken-rice.text: About this meal: Lemon and parsley lift the chicken, rice and soft cabbage without needing a salty sauce. Chicken provides protein and phosphorus, while rice makes it filling. It's a straightforward dinner with fresh flavours and a measured portion of each ingredient.

turkey-rosemary-rice.text: About this meal: Rosemary makes this turkey-and-rice dinner wonderfully homely, with carrot and cabbage adding colour. Turkey provides protein and phosphorus, while rice supplies carbohydrate. Cooking the vegetables simply lets their flavour come through without a salty stock cube.

pork-herb-rice.text: About this meal: Thyme and gently cooked cabbage are lovely with pork and rice. Pork provides a generous protein portion and contributes phosphorus, while the rice makes it satisfying. This is a good example of letting herbs do the seasoning instead of reaching for a packet sauce.

lemon-cod-rice.text: About this meal: Lemon and parsley keep this cod-and-rice meal light in flavour, while cabbage and onion make it satisfying. Cod provides protein and also contributes phosphorus. The olive oil supplies energy without having to rely on a creamy or salty sauce.

lemon-salmon-rice.text: About this meal: Salmon has a lovely richness of its own, especially with lemon and soft cabbage. It provides protein and beneficial omega-3 fats, and also contributes phosphorus. Rice gives the meal a simple carbohydrate base, so there's no need for an extra salty sauce to make it filling.

beef-paprika-rice.text: About this meal: Paprika and softened onion bring plenty of flavour to beef, rice and cabbage. Beef provides protein and phosphorus, while the rice gives the meal substance. Using fresh ingredients lets the spices do the work instead of a ready-made sauce, which can be useful if you watch salt.

egg-cheddar-pasta-cabbage.text: About this meal: Egg and Cheddar make this pasta rich and comforting, with cabbage adding a vegetable alongside. Both egg and cheese provide protein but also phosphorus; the recorded amount is worth noting if you manage it. Parsley brightens the sauce without needing extra cheese or salt.

creamy-pork-pasta-cabbage.text: About this meal: Cream and thyme turn pork pasta into a comforting dinner, with cabbage adding texture. Pork provides protein and phosphorus, while the cream supplies richness and energy. If your dietary advice includes managing saturated fat, it's worth recognising the role the cream plays in this particular meal.

egg-cauliflower-rice.text: About this meal: Eggs and Cheddar give this cauliflower rice bowl plenty of protein and flavour. Both also contribute phosphorus, so the fairly substantial figure is worth looking at if you monitor it. Cauliflower adds vegetables, while the basmati rice is the main carbohydrate component.

d011-creamy-chicken-mushroom-rice.text: About this meal: Mushrooms give this creamy chicken rice a deep savoury flavour without needing stock cubes or a packet sauce. Chicken provides protein, and both the mushrooms and cream contribute to the mineral totals. The potassium figure is worth checking if you've been asked to monitor it.

turkey-sweetcorn-pasta.text: About this meal: Turkey and sweetcorn make a comforting creamy pasta, with cabbage adding vegetables and lemon lifting the sauce. Turkey provides protein and phosphorus, while sweetcorn and pasta contribute carbohydrate. The complete serving has a meaningful potassium figure, so use that rather than judging the corn alone.

lemon-cod-pasta-peppers.text: About this meal: Lemon, parsley and green pepper bring freshness to this cod pasta. Fish supplies protein and phosphorus, while pasta provides carbohydrate. It's a simple way to enjoy a flavourful fish dinner without relying on a salty ready-made sauce.

pork-apple-rice-bowl.text: About this meal: Apple gives this pork and rice bowl a gentle sweetness, especially with rosemary and lemon. Pork provides protein and phosphorus, while cabbage adds vegetables. It's a lovely example of getting flavour from fruit and herbs instead of a sugary bottled glaze.

creamy-chicken-cabbage-pasta.text: About this meal: Creamy chicken pasta is a comforting dinner, and the cabbage brings some freshness and texture. Chicken supplies protein and phosphorus; the cream adds richness. A squeeze of lemon keeps the sauce lively without needing more salt.

egg-vegetable-pasta.text: About this meal: Egg, peppers and sweetcorn turn pasta into a colourful, satisfying meal without meat. Eggs provide protein and phosphorus, while the pasta and corn supply carbohydrate. Lemon and parsley add a fresh finish without relying on a salty sauce.

chicken-apple-couscous-style-rice.text: About this meal: Chicken, apple and cabbage make a pleasant sweet-savoury combination over rice. The chicken provides protein, while the apple and lemon lift the flavour naturally. Rice gives it substance, so the dish doesn't need a rich sauce to feel like a complete dinner.

beef-pepper-pasta.text: About this meal: Oregano and peppers bring a little Mediterranean warmth to beef pasta. Lean mince provides protein and phosphorus, and pasta makes the dish satisfying. Cooking the flavour into the vegetables avoids needing a salty packet sauce.

herb-cod-potatoes-cabbage.text: Potassium: Potatoes are a lovely match for lemony cod, but this serving contains a particularly substantial amount of potassium. The cooking method and potato portion matter, so use the recorded figure if you've been advised to limit potassium. Cod supplies useful protein alongside the cabbage.

creamy-cheese-egg-pasta.text: About this meal: Cheddar, milk and egg make this pasta wonderfully creamy, with onion adding sweetness. All three dairy-and-egg ingredients contribute to the phosphorus total, so it's a meal worth checking if you monitor phosphorus. Parsley brightens the sauce without needing extra cheese.

pork-apple-cabbage.text: About this meal: Pork and apple are a classic pairing, with cabbage making a comforting vegetable base. The pork supplies protein and phosphorus, while the apple brings sweetness without a bottled glaze. This dish has a meaningful potassium contribution, so check the recorded serving if potassium is one of your priorities.

creamy-chicken-pepper-pasta.text: About this meal: Thyme, peppers and onion give this creamy chicken pasta plenty of flavour. Chicken provides protein and phosphorus, while the cream adds richness. The vegetables add colour without needing a salty pasta sauce from a jar.

cod-sweetcorn-herb-pasta.text: About this meal: Cod, sweetcorn and parsley make a pleasant change from a creamy pasta dish. The cod provides protein and phosphorus; the pasta and corn supply carbohydrate. Lemon lifts the flavours, so the meal doesn't need a packet seasoning mix.

egg-cabbage-sweetcorn-rice.text: About this meal: Soft egg, sweetcorn and cabbage turn plain rice into a comforting, colourful bowl. Eggs give it protein and phosphorus, while rice and corn contribute carbohydrate. Onion and pepper provide flavour without soy sauce or salty meat.

pork-pepper-pasta.text: About this meal: Rosemary, peppers and onion are lovely with pork pasta, bringing plenty of savoury flavour without a bottled sauce. The pork provides a generous protein portion and contributes phosphorus. The recorded potassium and phosphorus totals are worth considering if you monitor either nutrient.

d030-pork-apple-cabbage-skillet.text: About this meal: Apple and rosemary make pork and cabbage taste wonderfully homely, with rice soaking up the flavours. Pork supplies protein, while apple brings a little sweetness without needing a glaze. The complete meal has a meaningful potassium contribution, so its total matters more than any single vegetable.

cheesy-egg-vegetable-rice.text: About this meal: Cheddar melts into egg-and-vegetable rice for a comforting, savoury bowl. Egg and cheese provide protein but also phosphorus, so the figure deserves a look if you monitor it. Sweetcorn and peppers add colour and sweetness without a bottled sauce.

cod-cabbage-pasta.text: About this meal: Cod and soft cabbage make a gentle, lemony pasta that's satisfying without cream. The fish supplies protein and phosphorus, while pasta provides carbohydrate. The recorded potassium is worth considering if you're monitoring it, rather than judging the cabbage in isolation.

pork-apple-herb-pasta.text: About this meal: Apple brings a lovely sweet note to pork pasta, especially with rosemary and onion. Pork provides plenty of protein and contributes phosphorus; the apple and pasta add carbohydrate in different forms. It's a satisfying dinner without needing a sweet bottled glaze.

egg-cauliflower-herb-pasta.text: About this meal: Cauliflower and onion add texture and sweetness to egg pasta, while parsley lifts the flavour. Eggs contribute protein and phosphorus, and the pasta makes it filling. The measured vegetables count towards the potassium figure, so check the complete meal if you monitor it.

d040-cod-sweetcorn-potato-bake.text: Potassium: Cod, sweetcorn and creamy potatoes make a comforting bake, but this is a particularly high-potassium serving because of the potato portion. If your team has advised limiting potassium, this is one to plan around using the recorded total. The fish provides protein, while the cream makes the sauce rich.

chicken-leek-couscous-lemon.text: About this meal: Lemon and parsley give chicken couscous a fresh, bright flavour, with leeks and carrots adding vegetables. Chicken contributes protein, though this particular serving is lighter in protein than many of the other chicken dinners. The couscous supplies the carbohydrate base.

cod-herby-noodles-cucumber.text: About this meal: Lemon and parsley brighten cod with soft noodles and crunchy cucumber. Cod supplies protein and phosphorus, and rice noodles make it satisfying without a heavy sauce. This is a relatively modest protein portion compared with some other fish dinners, so the number is worth noticing if you need more protein.

pork-apple-leek-rice.text: About this meal: Pork, apple and leek are a lovely sweet-savoury combination, with rice giving the meal substance. Thyme brings warmth without a bottled sauce. This serving has a modest protein amount compared with some larger meat dinners, which may matter depending on your own protein advice.

chicken-carrot-noodle-stir-fry.text: About this meal: Ginger makes chicken, carrot and cabbage noodles feel lively without a salty stir-fry sauce. The rice noodles provide carbohydrate and the chicken supplies protein. It's a comparatively light chicken portion, so check the protein figure if you're aiming for a higher-protein meal.

beef-meatballs-couscous-peppers.text: About this meal: Paprika and onion give these beef meatballs plenty of flavour, with couscous and pepper adding substance and colour. The beef provides protein, although the recorded portion is lighter than some meatball dishes. There's no need for a salty jar sauce to make this satisfying.

haddock-lemon-rice-leeks.text: About this meal: Haddock and lemon are a lovely combination, especially with soft leeks and rice. The fish provides protein and phosphorus, while carrots add colour. This is a lighter protein serving than some other fish recipes, so use the number shown if you're planning a higher-protein day.

chicken-pear-rice-bowl.text: About this meal: Pear gives this chicken rice bowl a gentle sweetness, with cabbage and rosemary keeping it savoury. Chicken supplies protein, while rice provides carbohydrate. It's a simple way to enjoy fruit in a main meal without relying on a sugary glaze.

pork-carrot-couscous-skillet.text: About this meal: Pork, carrot and leek make a satisfying couscous skillet with a gentle thyme flavour. The pork gives some protein and phosphorus, while the couscous supplies carbohydrate. It's a relatively light meat portion, useful to recognise if you've been advised to increase protein.

cod-leek-pasta-bake.text: About this meal: Cod and soft leeks make this pasta bake comforting without a heavy cheese sauce. Parsley adds flavour, and the fish contributes protein and phosphorus. The serving is lighter in protein than some other fish bakes, so the recorded number is useful if protein is a focus.

turkey-apple-noodle-bowl.text: About this meal: Turkey, apple and cucumber make a fresh noodle bowl, with ginger bringing warmth. Turkey contributes protein and rice noodles provide carbohydrate. The fruit-and-ginger combination means you don't need a sweet bottled sauce for flavour.

chicken-herb-meatballs-rice.text: About this meal: Chicken herb meatballs with rice and vegetables make a comforting dinner. Parsley adds freshness, while carrots and cabbage bring colour. The meatballs supply protein, though this recipe uses a smaller chicken portion than some others, so check the figure if your plan calls for more.

chicken-biryani-with-fragrant-basmati-ri.text: About this meal: Biryani gets its wonderful fragrance from saffron, mint and warming spices, with yoghurt keeping the chicken tender. Chicken provides a generous protein portion, while the basmati rice supplies carbohydrate. Tomato and yoghurt also contribute potassium, so the whole serving matters if you monitor it.

chicken-jalfrezi-with-chapati.text: About this meal: Jalfrezi has plenty of character from peppers, tomato, ginger and chilli, so it doesn't need a takeaway sauce. Chicken provides a generous protein portion and the chapati makes it satisfying. Tomato and peppers contribute potassium, which is worth knowing if you're managing it.

lamb-rogan-josh-with-rice.text: About this meal: Slow-cooked lamb and warm spices make rogan josh a rich, satisfying dinner with rice. Lamb and yoghurt provide protein and phosphorus, while the rice makes it substantial. The spices do the flavouring without needing a jarred curry sauce.

tandoori-style-fish-with-lemon-pilau.text: About this meal: Yoghurt, lemon and spices bring cod to life, with fragrant pilau rice alongside. The fish provides protein and phosphorus, while a little butter adds richness to the rice. It's full of flavour without needing a salty ready-made sauce.

chicken-karahi-with-homemade-flatbread.text: About this meal: Ginger, garlic and tomato give chicken karahi its lively flavour, with homemade flatbread to mop up the sauce. Chicken provides plenty of protein, while tomato and the other vegetables contribute potassium. The combination can be enjoyed thoughtfully without treating tomato as forbidden.

coconut-fish-curry-with-rice.text: About this meal: Coconut milk, curry leaves and tamarind make this fish curry rich and fragrant. Haddock provides protein, while coconut milk adds fat and energy; the rice makes it satisfying. The spices bring enough character that there's no need for a salty jar sauce.

chicken-shish-tawook-with-vermicelli-ric.text: About this meal: Lemon and garlic give shish tawook plenty of flavour, while vermicelli rice and fresh cucumber salad round out the plate. Chicken provides a generous protein portion. Tomato and yoghurt also contribute potassium, so the recorded whole serving is useful if that's something you monitor.

homemade-chicken-pide.text: About this meal: Homemade chicken pide is a lovely way to enjoy spiced chicken and vegetables on warm bread. Chicken and egg make it protein-rich, while the bread supplies carbohydrate. Tomato and peppers bring freshness without a bottled topping.

saffron-chicken-with-jewelled-rice.text: About this meal: Saffron and citrus make the chicken fragrant, while carrot, raisins and almonds bring colour and sweetness to the rice. Chicken supplies protein, and nuts add plant fats and some phosphorus. Raisins also contribute potassium, so their measured portion matters if you monitor it.

chicken-gyros-platter.text: About this meal: Oregano, garlic and lemon make these chicken gyros delicious, with warm pitta, potatoes and cooling yoghurt alongside. Chicken provides plenty of protein, and the potato portion contributes potassium. If you're following potassium advice, pay attention to how much potato is included, rather than assuming a gyros platter is automatically unsuitable.

chicken-and-apricot-tagine.text: About this meal: Apricots and warming spices give this chicken tagine its lovely sweet-savoury character, with couscous soaking up the juices. Dried apricots contribute potassium, so the measured amount matters if you monitor it. Almonds add crunch and some phosphorus.

spiced-lamb-and-vegetable-pastilla.text: About this meal: Crisp filo pastry and fragrant lamb make this pastilla a special-occasion dinner, with almonds adding richness and crunch. Lamb and egg provide protein and phosphorus, while pastry and butter make it energy-rich. It's a delicious choice to enjoy with the portion in mind.

harissa-style-baked-fish-with-couscous.text: About this meal: Chilli, caraway and lemon make harissa-style fish lively without needing a bottled sauce. Haddock provides protein, while couscous supplies carbohydrate. Tomato purée adds depth but also contributes potassium, so it's worth noting if you monitor that nutrient.

sweet-and-sour-chicken-with-rice.text: About this meal: Fresh pineapple, peppers and vinegar give sweet-and-sour chicken its bright flavour without a bottled sauce. Chicken and egg provide a generous amount of protein, while rice and the crisp coating add carbohydrate. The sweetness comes partly from sugar, so include the sauce if you're counting carbohydrates.

ginger-and-spring-onion-steamed-fish.text: About this meal: Ginger and spring onion are wonderful with gently steamed cod, and cabbage keeps the rice plate fresh. The fish provides protein and phosphorus. Soy sauce adds salt to the cooking juices, so measuring it is useful if you're managing sodium.

crispy-pork-with-garlic-noodles.text: About this meal: Crispy pork belly and garlicky noodles make a rich, satisfying dinner, with Chinese cabbage adding crunch. Pork belly provides plenty of fat and energy alongside protein. Soy sauce adds salt, so the measured amount is worth noting if you're keeping an eye on sodium.

chicken-teriyaki-style-rice-bowl.text: About this meal: A homemade teriyaki-style glaze gives chicken rice a glossy, sweet-savoury finish, with cucumber and carrot keeping it fresh. Soy sauce contributes salt and the glaze contains sugar. If you're counting carbohydrate, remember that the sauce contributes alongside the rice.

thai-basil-chicken-with-jasmine-rice.text: About this meal: Basil, chilli and garlic make this minced-chicken rice fragrant and lively. Chicken provides a generous portion of protein, while jasmine rice makes it filling. Fish sauce and soy sauce both contribute salt, so the amounts in the recipe are worth keeping in mind.

red-curry-style-chicken-with-rice.text: About this meal: Lemongrass, galangal and coconut milk give this curry its distinctive fragrance, with pepper and beans adding colour. Chicken supplies protein, while coconut milk makes the sauce rich. Fish sauce contributes salt, so its measured amount matters if you're watching sodium.

lemongrass-pork-with-rice-noodles.text: About this meal: Lemongrass and lime make these pork noodles wonderfully fresh, with pickled vegetables and herbs providing crunch. Pork supplies protein and phosphorus, while fish sauce adds the characteristic savoury note and some salt. The rice noodles provide a satisfying carbohydrate base.

chicken-laksa-inspired-noodle-bowl.text: About this meal: This laksa-inspired bowl is rich with coconut milk, ginger and lemongrass, with chicken and noodles making it filling. Chicken provides protein, while coconut milk adds richness. Fish sauce contributes salt, so the measured amount is worth remembering if you're managing sodium.

chicken-enchiladas-with-homemade-sauce.text: About this meal: Homemade tomato-and-chilli sauce gives these chicken enchiladas plenty of flavour, with Cheddar adding a melting finish.
